title: Audio Track Harmonizer
description:
A digital audio workstation features an auto-stitching tool designed to bridge gaps in a podcast episode. To fill a gap of exactly `target_duration` seconds, the system needs to pick exactly two distinct audio clips from a sound library. You are given an array of positive integers `durations`, where each element represents the duration of a sound clip in seconds, and an integer `target_duration`. Return the 0-based indices of the two audio clips whose total duration equals `target_duration`.

You may assume that each input has exactly one valid pair of clips, and you cannot use the same audio clip twice. The indices in the returned array can be in any order.
input_format: An integer array durations and an integer target_duration.
output_format: An array of two integers [i, j] representing the 0-based indices of the selected clips.

examples.explanation: The clip at index 1 (180 seconds) and the clip at index 2 (240 seconds) sum up to 180 + 240 = 420 seconds.
The array contains only two clips, and their durations (150 + 150) equal the target duration of 300 seconds.
The clip at index 0 (45 seconds) and the clip at index 4 (225 seconds) add up to 45 + 225 = 270 seconds.
